newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Macraes cuts dividend to fund expansion.
newsitem.headline: Macraes cuts dividend to fund expansion.

text.p: Macraes Mining Company said on Thursday it was cutting its annual dividend to help fund the expansion of its Macraes gold mine which will triple treatment capacity to nine million tonnes of throughput per year.
The new plant will represent an investment of NZ$120 million.
The Macraes mine is near Dunedin in New Zealand's South Island. The company said the higher throughput would yield between 320,000 and 350,000 ounces of gold annually.
The company reported an annual net profit of NZ$15.44 million, up 118 percent from the previous year's $7.09 million.
It said its record-breaking performance had focused on the core business drivers of increasing revenues, cash margins and gold output.
During the year the company produced 138,464 ounces of gold, generating a 12.6 percent increase in sales at NZ$94.5 million.
A full year's cash operating margin of NZ$299 per ounce was locked in place due to the company's extensive forward-selling programme, together with decreased cash cost per ounce.
A cash cost per ounce of NZ$358 in the December quarter and NZ$402 for the full year was the lowest since production began in 1990. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
